entry_updates.mechanism_append: Cancellation helpers make the collection's generation/caller rule precise. `combineAbortSignals` drops undefined inputs, returns no signal for zero inputs, reuses the single input unchanged, and creates a controller for multiple inputs. The first observed abort preserves its reason; an already aborted input stops listener registration at that input, and the explicit cleanup closure removes every listener installed earlier. It does not cancel the input controllers. `raceWithAbortSignal` rejects an already aborted waiter while attaching a catch to the operation, otherwise settles once on operation completion/failure or abort and removes its listener. It checks again after listener installation to close the registration race. The operation remains observed after waiter cancellation; this helper does not stop its side effects. An undefined abort reason becomes Error('The operation was aborted') with name AbortError (ice:packages/ai/src/utils/abort-signals.ts:1-41; ice:packages/ai/src/utils/abort.ts:1-50).
entry_updates.interfaces_append: `CombinedAbortSignal { signal?: AbortSignal; cleanup: () => void }`; `combineAbortSignals(signals: readonly (AbortSignal | undefined)[]): CombinedAbortSignal`; `raceWithAbortSignal<T>(operation: Promise<T>, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<T>`. `ModelsRequestTransforms.transformHeaders?: (headers: ProviderHeaders) => ProviderHeaders | Promise<ProviderHeaders>` is intersected into raw/simple/deferred collection request option types (ice:packages/ai/src/models.ts:78-86).

Exported symbols: `calculateCost` (ice:packages/ai/src/models.ts:878).
Exported symbols: `KnownApi`, `KnownProvider`, `GrammarFormat`, `GrammarVariants`, `ModelCostRates`, `ModelCostTier`, `ModelCost` (ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:16; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:34; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:488; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:490; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:791; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:798; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:803).
entry_updates.mechanism_append: The exported `calculateCost(model, usage)` selects rates using total billable input `usage.input + usage.cacheRead + usage.cacheWrite`. It chooses the largest tier threshold strictly exceeded, starting matchedThreshold at -1. It mutates and returns the existing `usage.cost`: input/output/cacheRead are their counts times the respective per-million rates; cacheWrite is `(rates.cacheWrite * (usage.cacheWrite - (usage.cacheWrite1h ?? 0)) + rates.input * 2 * (usage.cacheWrite1h ?? 0)) / 1_000_000`; total sums the four resulting components. There is no validation or clamping of malformed numeric counters in this helper (ice:packages/ai/src/models.ts:878-897).
entry_updates.rust_append: The native `calculate_cost` preserves the same strict highest-threshold rule and ordinary cost arithmetic, returning a new UsageCost instead of mutating the input. It clamps long cache-write count to at least zero and short cache writes to at least zero, unlike TS for inconsistent/negative counters. Retain this explicit native defensive behavior unless a malformed-input compatibility requirement is chosen; the ordinary valid-input calculation is already implemented (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/anthropic/cost.rs:17-48).

entry_updates.source_append: Exported symbols: `ChatTemplateKwargValue`, `OpenAIResponsesCompat`, `AnthropicMessagesCompat`, `BedrockCompat`, `OpenRouterRouting`, `VercelGatewayRouting` (ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:83; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:625; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:643; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:699; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:710; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:784).
entry_updates.interfaces_append: The public runtime type names are `ChatTemplateKwargValue`, `OpenAIResponsesCompat`, `AnthropicMessagesCompat`, `BedrockCompat`, `OpenRouterRouting`, and `VercelGatewayRouting`. The Bedrock runtime record has only optional `supportsStrictMode?: boolean`; it is not a separately tagged arm of the models.json compatibility union. The other runtime-only declaration differences, including supportsExplicitPromptCacheMode, remain as documented above (ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:83-91; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:625-789).

entry_updates.mechanism_append: Before wire serialization, `sanitizeSurrogates(text)` removes unpaired UTF-16 high surrogates and unpaired low surrogates using a non-Unicode global regular expression; it preserves valid surrogate pairs and all other text. This helper is a request-text projection and does not rewrite persisted messages (ice:packages/ai/src/utils/sanitize-unicode.ts:21-24).
entry_updates.rust_append: Native `String` already excludes lone surrogate code points. Anthropic therefore implements its named sanitizer as a pass-through, while the image adapter's scalar filter cannot encounter a surrogate in a valid `&str`; these are representation differences, not a missing native text-cleaning feature (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/anthropic/build_params.rs:704-709; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/images.rs:426-433).

entry_updates.mechanism_append: `validateToolCall` chooses the first tool whose name exactly equals `toolCall.name`, throws `Tool "<name>" not found` when absent, and then calls `validateToolArguments`. `StringEnum(values, options?)` constructs a Type.Unsafe primitive schema `{ type: 'string', enum: values }`; it preserves the supplied value array and includes description/default only when each is truthy, so an empty-string default is omitted. It performs no deduplication or separate value validation. This is schema construction, not a bypass of the subsequent execution validator (ice:packages/ai/src/utils/validation.ts:270-275; ice:packages/ai/src/utils/typebox-helpers.ts:14-23).
